subject: TTFT & streaming requirements - follow-up from demo (Aperture AI)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: TTFT & streaming requirements - follow-up from demo (Aperture AI)

Hi Henry - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

Call recap
- Use case: Real-time assistant in Aperture's product UI (chunked streaming responses, immediate token render).
- Primary perf SLOs you mentioned: strong Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) expectations for interactive feel, and steady chunk cadence for streaming.

What I captured as your targets (please confirm):
- TTFT: p95 <= 250 ms (ideal target p95 <= 200 ms)
- p50: ~120 ms
- Concurrency: 150-200 sustained concurrent active users, burst up to 500
- Throughput: target ~5k tokens/sec across cluster during peak (we'll validate)
- Streaming: client uses WebSocket (preferred) but SSE is acceptable - chunk cadence target <= 200 ms, ideally ~100-150 ms between chunks; small chunk size for incremental rendering (<= 256 bytes of payload).

Action items / next steps
1) Dev to run an initial benchmark (baseline + concurrency ramp) and share results (Marissa/Dev) - goal: reproduce TTFT numbers and streaming chunk cadence.
2) I'll send the SLA template and MA plan for review.
3) Schedule PoC: propose a 2-week PoC with dedicated capacity to validate TTFT at your concurrency profile.

Attachments: demo slides attached.

Would you confirm the targets above (TTFT p95 / concurrency / preferred streaming protocol) and share average response length (typical tokens per response) so we can size the benchmark appropriately?

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Henry Thompson <henry.thompson@apertureai.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming requirements - follow-up from demo (Aperture AI)

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. Confirming and adding a few clarifications: 

Confirmed targets
- TTFT: please treat p95 <= 250 ms as our SLA target. If you can hit p95 <= 200 ms that's excellent.
- p50: ~120 ms (helps with perceived latency for most users).
- Concurrency: 200 sustained concurrent sessions; system should tolerate 500 concurrent during peaks without severe degradation.
- Throughput: goal of ~5k tokens/sec aggregated across the service during peak.
- Streaming: we prefer WebSocket for lower-latency bidirectional work, but SSE is acceptable for a first PoC. Chunk cadence: aim for 100-150 ms between chunks, but anything <= 250 ms is a pass. Chunk payloads should be small enough for incremental render - sub-256 bytes preferable.

Other notes/questions
- Average response length: ranges 80-300 tokens (median ~140 tokens). We have a few long responses up to ~1k tokens but those are rare.
- We care about p99 as well for burst scenarios (we'd like to see p99 documented).
- Security/residency: our legal team will need the SLA + data residency language (US-only) included in the template you send.

If you can draft a PoC plan that includes an initial benchmarking script (single-client baseline, concurrent ramp to 200, burst to 500) and a streaming cadence measurement, we can lock dates next week.

Thanks -
Henry Thompson
Head of Platform, Aperture AI
henry.thompson@apertureai.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Henry Thompson <henry.thompson@apertureai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-26T02:40:00Z
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming requirements - follow-up from demo (Aperture AI)

On Fri, Jun 25, 2027 at 17:05 Henry Thompson <henry.thompson@apertureai.com> wrote:
> Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. Confirming and adding a few clarifications: ...

Hi Henry - Dev (SE) here. Appreciate the specifics - that helps a lot. A few technical clarifications so our benchmark matches your workload: 

Questions
1) Response size distribution: you mentioned median ~140 tokens, 80-300 typical, rare 1k. Can you share percentile breakdown if available (p50/p90/p99 tokens)? If not, median + a couple of representative long samples will do.
2) Streaming format: WebSocket + newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) or binary frames? If you have an existing client expectation (e.g., SSE with "data:" frames vs JSON-chunked WS), please tell us. For PoC we'll support both and compare.
3) Reconnections: do you have client-side reconnection/backoff behavior requirements? For example, if network blips cause dropped WS, should server attempt resume using KV cache tokens?

Proposed benchmark plan
- Step 0: baseline cold-start TTFT with single client (3 runs avg) to establish p50/p95/p99.
- Step 1: steady-state test at target concurrency (200) over 30 minutes to observe TTFT, throughput, and chunk cadence.
- Step 2: burst test (500 concurrent for 5 minutes) to validate graceful degradation/fallback.
- Step 3: streaming cadence measurement: measure inter-chunk arrival times (ms) and chunk sizes (bytes) across runs; capture percentiles.
- Step 4: token throughput measurement (tokens/sec) and CPU/GPU utilization sampling.

Deliverables
- Raw CSV results (sample attached), summarized p50/p95/p99 TTFT and chunk cadence, suggested config to meet p95 target (batching, quantization profile, routing).

Scheduling
- We can run the PoC bench next Tue/Wed (UTC-7) if that works for you.

I'll attach a small baseline results CSV and the harness script after we confirm response-size samples.

Thanks -
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
